title.en: The Sun and the Moon (A Traditional Tale)

summaryEn: A gentle, simplified retelling of the traditional Korean folk tale Haenim Dallim: a brother and sister outwit a tricky tiger, climb a rope into the sky, and become the sun and the moon.
learningGoalsEn: Recognize Haenim Dallim as a traditional Korean folk tale told in many versions, and this retelling as a simplified one.
Retell the main events: the tricky tiger, the tree, the rope from the sky, the sun and the moon.
Recognize and say 해, 달, 호랑이, 떡 and 동아줄.
Notice that folk tales sometimes 'explain' nature (why sorghum stalks are red) as part of the story, not as science.

origin.noteEn: One version of a traditional tale; the Sources screen lists the versions this retelling follows.
origin.retellingNoteEn: Shortened and made gentler; versions differ.

review.advisoryNoteEn: A trickster and a moment of danger, told gently; the scariest parts are left out.

keywords.en: the Sun and the Moon (with the respectful ending -nim; the tale's title)

scenes.narrationEn: Story time with Hoya! This is an old Korean folk tale, told in many versions. It is called Haenim Dallim, The Sun and the Moon. Our retelling is simplified and gentler than the old tellings. And the tiger is a trickster, not like me!

keyword.en: the Sun and the Moon (with the respectful ending -nim; the tale's title)

scenes.artBrief: Hoya sitting cross-legged with an open folding screen behind him painted with a sun, a moon and mountains, winking at the viewer.

scenes.narrationEn: Long ago, a mother went out to work. Heading home with rice cakes, she met a tiger at a hill pass. 'Give me your rice cakes!' it said. The old tale has it ask for more at each hill. We keep it short.
scenes.artBrief: A winding hilltop path at sunset; a mother in hanbok with a covered bundle of rice cakes, and a comical roly-poly tiger with no scary teeth peeking from behind a boulder; a thatched cottage far below.

scenes.narrationEn: The tiger went to the children's house, pretending to be Mother. 'Open the door!' The children said, 'Your voice and hand are not Mother's!' But when the tiger said it must feed the crying baby, they opened the door.
scenes.artBrief: A cottage door slightly ajar at dusk, two children peeking out with wide eyes; only a fuzzy striped paw and a shawl are visible outside, drawn comically rather than scary.

scenes.narrationEn: Then the children realized it was the tiger, and they climbed a tall tree beside the well. Hoya whispers: 'Don't worry, it's only a story, and these two are clever!'
scenes.artBrief: Two children perched high in a big tree beside a stone well under starlight, looking down calmly; a striped tail just visible behind the cottage; Hoya in a corner of the frame giving a thumbs-up.

scenes.narrationEn: 'How did you get up there?' asked the tiger. The clever brother said, 'Rub on some sesame oil!' Slip, slide, bump! The tiger couldn't climb. But soon it found another way up.
scenes.artBrief: The tiger sliding comically down a shiny tree trunk with a little oil bottle beside it, the children giggling behind their hands.

scenes.narrationEn: The children prayed to the sky: 'Please send down a new rope!' A strong new rope came down, and up they climbed. The tiger tried a rope too, but it was old and rotten. Snap!

line.en: Please send down a new rope.
line.speaker: narrator

scenes.artBrief: A thick golden rope descending from glowing clouds as the two children climb it; far below, a frayed grey rope snapping near the treetops.

scenes.narrationEn: Down tumbled the tiger into a field of sorghum, and that was the end of its tricks. Storytellers say that is why sorghum stalks are red! The tale even has another name: 'Why Sorghum Stalks Are Red.'
scenes.artBrief: A field of tall reddish sorghum stalks swaying, with only the tip of a striped tail sticking out among them; soft, funny mood.

scenes.narrationEn: In the sky, the brother became the sun and the sister the moon. But she was scared of the dark night, so they swapped. Shy of people staring, the sister-sun shines so brightly that no one can look at her. They are safe and sound!
scenes.artBrief: A split sky: a warm smiling sun with the sister's face on one side and a gentle moon with the brother's face on the other, over sleeping mountains; Hoya waving goodbye.

checks.promptEn: At the first hill pass, what did the tiger ask the mother for?
What came down from the sky to help the children?
Why did the sister and brother swap places in the sky?

options.en: She wanted to see the sunrise
She was afraid of the dark night
She felt the sun was too hot
Her brother asked to shine first

facts.claimEn: 'The Brother and Sister Who Became the Sun and the Moon' (also called Haenim Dallim) is a traditional Korean folk tale (mindam) told widely across the country, with many variant versions.
facts.claimKo: 「해와 달이 된 오누이」(｢해님달님｣)는 전국적으로 널리 전승되는 민담이며 여러 변이형이 있다.

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정의: ‘남매가 호랑이의 위협을 피하여 하늘로 올라가 해와 달이 된 내용의 민담.’ / 개설: ‘전국적으로 널리 전승되며, ｢해님달님｣ · ｢일월전설(日月傳說)｣ · ｢수숫대가 빨간 이유｣라고도 부른다.’ / 현황: ‘각편의 여러 변이형 가운데에는 …’

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이 (한국민속문학사전)
sources.publisher: 국립민속박물관 (National Folk Museum of Korea) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 분석: ‘한국에서는 ‘해와 달이 된 오누이’ 또는 ‘해님 달님’ 등의 제목으로 널리 구전되어 왔다.’ / 변이: ‘민담화되면서 이 이야기에는 많은 변이들이 발생한다.’

facts.claimEn: In the tale, a mother who has been out working meets a tiger on her way home. In the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture's basic version the tiger appears at one hill pass after another and makes demands in turn, rice cakes first and then more; this retelling keeps only the rice cakes and leaves out the rest.
facts.claimKo: 이야기에서 품일을 나갔던 어머니가 돌아오는 길에 호랑이를 만난다. 대백과사전의 기본형에서는 호랑이가 고개마다 나타나 떡을 시작으로 차례로 여러 가지를 요구하는데, 이 재구성은 첫 번째인 떡만 남기고 나머지는 줄였다.

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이
sources.quoteOrLocator: 내용: ‘옛날에 한 어머니가 삼 남매를 집에 두고 품일을 나갔다가 돌아오는 길에 호랑이를 만났다. 호랑이는 고개마다 나타나서 어머니에게 떡, 옷, 팔, 다리, 몸통을 차례로 요구한 뒤 …’

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이 (한국민속문학사전)
sources.publisher: 국립민속박물관 (National Folk Museum of Korea) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 줄거리: ‘호랑이가 이웃 부잣집에 품일을 갔다 오던 늙은 어머니를 잡아먹고는 …’ (a shorter version of the same opening: the mother is returning from working at a neighbor's house)

facts.claimEn: In the Encyclopedia's basic version, the tiger goes to the children's house pretending to be their mother; the children say the voice and hand are not their mother's and refuse to open the door, but open it when the tiger says it must nurse the crying baby; the siblings then realize who it is and flee up a big tree beside the well. Other versions differ (in the National Folk Museum's summary the children look through a hole in the door, see the tiger, and escape by the back door to a tree). This retelling is simplified.
facts.claimKo: 대백과사전의 기본형에서 호랑이는 어머니인 척 아이들의 집에 찾아간다. 아이들은 목소리와 손바닥이 어머니와 다르다며 문을 열어 주지 않다가 호랑이가 우는 젖먹이에게 젖을 먹여야 한다고 하자 문을 열어 주고, 곧 호랑이의 정체를 알아차려 우물가 큰 나무 위로 피한다. 각편에 따라 다르며(국립민속박물관 줄거리에서는 문구멍으로 내다보고 호랑이인 줄 알아 뒷문으로 도망쳐 나무 위로 피한다), 이 재구성은 단순화한 것이다.

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘아이들은 호랑이의 목소리와 손바닥이 어머니와 다르다고 문을 열어 주지 않았으나, 호랑이가 우는 젖먹이에게 젖을 먹여야 한다고 하자 문을 열어 주었다. 호랑이가 젖먹이를 잡아먹자 남매는 호랑이 정체를 알아차리고 겨우 도망하여 우물가 큰 나무 위로 피신했다.’

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이 (한국민속문학사전)
sources.publisher: 국립민속박물관 (National Folk Museum of Korea) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 줄거리: ‘오누이는 문구멍으로 내다보고는 호랑이인 줄 알고 뒷문으로 도망쳐 나무 위로 피한다.’

facts.claimEn: In the Encyclopedia's basic version, following the brother's advice the tiger rubs on sesame oil and fails to climb the tree, then finds another way up (the sister's advice).
facts.claimKo: 대백과사전의 기본형에서 호랑이는 오빠의 말대로 참기름을 바르고 나무에 오르려다 실패하고, 이후 누이가 일러 준 다른 방법으로 올라간다.

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘처음에는 오빠의 말대로 참기름을 바르고 나무에 오르려다 실패하고, 그 다음에는 누이가 일러 준 대로 도끼로 나무를 찍으며 올라갔다.’ (the axe detail is left out of this retelling)

facts.claimEn: In the tale, the siblings pray to the sky for a rope; a new, strong rope (dongajul) comes down and they climb up, while the tiger takes a rotten rope that breaks.
facts.claimKo: 남매가 하늘에 동아줄을 내려 달라고 빌자 새 동아줄이 내려와 하늘로 오르고, 호랑이가 잡은 썩은 동아줄은 끊어진다.

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘남매는 하늘에 동아줄을 내려 달라고 기원하여 하늘에서 내려온 새 동아줄을 타고 하늘로 올라갔고, 호랑이는 하늘에서 내려온 썩은 동아줄을 잡고 하늘로 오르다가 동아줄이 끊어져 수수밭에 떨어졌다.’

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이 (한국민속문학사전)
sources.publisher: 국립민속박물관 (National Folk Museum of Korea) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 줄거리: ‘오누이는 하늘에 빌어 하늘에서 내려준 쇠줄을 타고 올라가 … 호랑이도 오누이를 쫓아 썩은 동아줄을 타고 하늘에 오르다가 줄이 끊어져 …’ / 변이: ‘“살려주시려면 굵은 동아줄을, 죽이시려면 썩은 동아줄을 내려주세요.”라는 오누이의 기원’

sources.title: 동아줄
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language) — 표준국어대사전

facts.claimEn: In the tale, the tiger falls from the rotten rope into a sorghum field, and storytellers use this to explain why sorghum stalks are red; some versions keep only the red-sorghum explanation, and the tale is also known as 'Why Sorghum Stalks Are Red'.
facts.claimKo: 호랑이는 썩은 줄이 끊어져 수수밭에 떨어지고, 이야기는 이것으로 수숫대가 붉은 까닭을 설명한다. 수숫대가 붉어진 유래만 이야기하는 각편도 있으며, 이 설화는 ｢수숫대가 빨간 이유｣라고도 불린다.

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘동아줄이 끊어져 수수밭에 떨어졌다.’ / ‘수수가 붉게 되었다.’ / 개설: ‘｢수숫대가 빨간 이유｣라고도 부른다.’

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이 (한국민속문학사전)
sources.publisher: 국립민속박물관 (National Folk Museum of Korea) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 변이: ‘호랑이의 추락과 죽음으로 인해 수숫대가 붉어진 유래담도 형성되었다.’ / ‘해와 달에 관한 기원담은 생략되고 수숫대가 붉게 된 유래만 내용으로 삼는 유형도 있다.’

facts.claimEn: In the basic version, the brother first becomes the sun and the sister the moon, but because the sister is afraid of the night they swap. The sister, now the sun, is shy of people looking at her: the Encyclopedia says she pricks at people's eyes with needles so they cannot look straight at the sun, while the National Folk Museum's summary says she gives off a strong light. This retelling uses only the gentler 'too bright to look at' version. Versions differ (in some, the brother stays the sun).
facts.claimKo: 기본형에서 오빠는 해, 누이는 달이 되었으나 누이가 밤을 무서워해 서로 바꾸었고, 해가 된 누이는 사람들이 쳐다보는 것이 부끄러워 사람들이 해를 똑바로 볼 수 없게 되었다. 대백과사전은 누이가 바늘로 눈을 콕콕 찌른다고 설명하고, 국립민속박물관 줄거리는 강력한 빛을 뿜는다고 설명하는데, 이 재구성은 순한 쪽(너무 밝아서 볼 수 없음)만 따랐다. 각편마다 다르다(오빠가 그대로 해가 되는 유형도 있다).

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘오빠는 해가 되고 누이는 달이 되었다. 그런데 누이가 밤이 무섭다고 하여 오빠가 바꿔 주어 누이는 해가 되고 오빠는 달이 되었다. 해가 된 누이는 낮에 사람들이 쳐다보는 것이 부끄러워 자신을 못 보게 바늘로 콕콕 찔러서 사람들이 해를 똑바로 쳐다볼 수 없게 되었다.’

sources.title: 해와 달이 된 오누이 (한국민속문학사전)
sources.publisher: 국립민속박물관 (National Folk Museum of Korea) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 줄거리: ‘하느님이 오빠는 해, 동생은 달이 되게 하였지만 동생이 밤이 무섭다고 하여 역할을 바꾸어 오빠는 달, 여동생은 해가 된다. 여동생은 낮에 사람들이 쳐다보는 것이 부끄러워 강력한 빛을 뿜어낸다.’ / 변이: ‘누이가 무섭다고 해도 오빠가 한 번 정해진 것을 바꿀 수가 없다고 하여 오빠가 해가 되는 유형도 있다.’

referenceDisplay: Traditional folk tale, one version retold gently and simplified (versions differ). As told in: 한국민족문화대백과사전 「해와 달이 된 오누이」 (한국학중앙연구원) and 한국민속문학사전 「해와 달이 된 오누이」 (국립민속박물관); 국립국어원 표준국어대사전. Not history.

verification.notes: Third independent pass over 6 episodes / 61 facts / 161 source entries (70 unique URLs). Every URL was re-fetched with my own scripts (UNESCO pages via Wayback copies; heritage.go.kr descriptions via the portal ajax html and khs.go.kr open API; folkency via its JSON API) and each quote or locator was machine-matched to the page text; the few non-matching strings were checked by hand (portal metadata fields, hanja or footnote punctuation, label text). Corrections: (1) pansori scene 2 now gives both UNESCO steps (2003 masterpiece proclamation, 2008 Representative List); (2) pansori f11 states the Aesop title as in the cited Townsend text and the common alternate title; (3) added sources: NFM 놀보박타령 for 'greedy' (f5), 표준국어대사전 타다 for 'sawed' (f6), 한국민족문화대백과사전 선도해 for the Samguk sagi tale (f12); (4) Seollal f9/f10 designation-date locators now cite the KHS open API field. No other change. See seasons-tales.signoff.md.

authorNotes: REVISED 2026-10-10. Traditional tale: narration describes what happens in the tale, not history. Two authoritative sources now: the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (E0062663; basic version with three siblings) and the National Folk Museum's 한국민속문학사전 entry by 조현설 (topic 6006; summary with two children, whose folk-literature dictionary cites 한국구비문학대계 1-4, 811; 1-5, 308; 2-6, 473; 2-7, 513 as its sources - the 구비문학대계 recordings themselves could not be opened with the tools used, gubi.aks.ac.kr returned nothing). The sesame-oil episode (f4) rests on the Encyclopedia only (the NFM summary does not mention it); claims kept minimal. Differences between sources, stated openly in the facts: Encyclopedia - mother met at successive hill passes with demands rice cake, clothes, arms, legs, torso; children open the door when the tiger says it must nurse the baby; the sun-sister pricks people's eyes with needles. NFM - children see the tiger through a hole in the door and flee by the back door; the sun-sister gives off a strong light. This retelling follows the gentler options where they exist. Softened on purpose: the tiger eating the mother and the baby; the demands for clothes, arms, legs and torso; the axe; the tiger's death on the sorghum stalks (told as 'the end of its tricks'); the needles. Three siblings (삼 남매) in the Encyclopedia vs. two (오누이) in the NFM summary: narration says 'the children' and mentions the crying baby only because the tiger uses it as an excuse. 님 is a gender-neutral respectful suffix; in this retelling the sun is the sister and the moon the brother, so the 'Mr. Sun, Ms. Moon' gloss was removed. Reassurance beats added in scenes 4, 7 and 8. The line '떡 하나 주면 안 잡아먹지' is not used (not in the sources; too scary for young children). Hoya's 'not like me!' is character banter. Stage 5 'Tiger Folktales' is a natural placement, but the language is at Listen level, hence recommended_stage 1.
